title: Router Windows App Design
eyebrow: Design for approval · replaces the build plan page, nothing built yet

short.lead: You keep the website and also get a Windows app you install once. Both use the same board. The app can do what a website can't: it finds your Claude folders without asking, turns on limit tracking itself, and starts or resumes local sessions in a terminal. One correction to your message: the website already reads local sessions, as long as you show it each folder once. It just can't find folders or start sessions.
short.hint: Tap an item to see what it creates and what it needs from you.
items: The board, its cards and its three bars (context, 5-hour limit and weekly limit) are written once. The website and the app both show the same thing.

items: The app looks in your user folder for every folder named .claude or starting with .claude-, and lists them in the walkthrough for you to confirm.
Resume opens Windows Terminal in the project folder with that session reopened on its own account. New session opens one on the account you choose.
A green dot and the words "running now" mark sessions that have a Claude process open on your PC.
A fresh build plan and issues follow, then the build.

changes: new
Windows app
An installer from GitHub Releases that adds the router to your Start menu.

The app is the website's board inside its own window, plus a small helper program with permission to read your folders and open terminals. Each new version is built and tested on GitHub's own Windows machines, so the Windows parts get tested on real Windows before you get them. The installer isn't signed, so the first time you run it Windows shows a "Windows protected your PC" warning. Click "More info", then "Run anyway". Removing the warning needs a paid code-signing certificate.
Only the website is planned.
An installed app with the same board.
Setup is a confirm screen, and sessions start from the board.
new
Start and resume
The app opens sessions for you.
Resume runs claude --resume with that session's ID, in its project folder, on the account it was made with. New session here asks which account to use.
You open a terminal and type the commands yourself.
Buttons on each card and on each project.
Getting back into a project takes one click.

choices: What should the Windows app be built with?
Electron (the website in its own app window, with a built-in copy of Chrome)
It reuses the website's code as it is, and I can run it here. The download is roughly 100 MB (exact size only known once built), because it bundles its own copy of Chrome.
Tauri (the website in its own app window, using the browser engine Windows already has)

It uses the Edge engine that Windows already has, so the download is roughly 10 MB (a typical Tauri app size; the exact size is only known once built). Its back end is written in Rust, and I can only test the Windows build on GitHub's machines, not here.
The website plus a small helper program

The website stays the only screen, and a small installed helper gives it access to your files and terminals. It is the smallest download, but browsers make websites ask permission before talking to programs on your PC, which adds a prompt.

Option A is the quickest route to something that works, it's tested here and on Windows, and size matters little for an app you install once. (Both sizes are typical figures for apps of each kind; the real size is only known once built.)
When you start a new session, which account should it use?
The one with the most room, picked for you
The window shows each account's limits with the emptiest one already picked, and you can change it.
Fastest, but it can land you on an account that is nearly out of limit.
Option A is the routing part of the project's goal: it steers work to the account that has room, without making you check each one.
One pull request that has the board, the website and the Windows app.
As in the current build plan. The app follows later.
Building both together costs little more than building one first, because most of the work is the shared board.
